To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel approach to reconstruct events on file system metadata, that is applicable to any kind of file system, and that we have implemented a prototype that is able to reconstruct the events on the basis of a single file system image, without any additional input or knowledge.

1) we introduce a novel forensic approach for reconstructing past events on a computer, without relying on any knowledge about the operating system, specific applications, or file formats; 2) we provide a prototype implementation of this approach, which we evaluated with real data; 3) the evaluation shows, that the approach is able to reconstruct events, and that it is feasible for forensic investigations.

1) it is possible to automatically reconstruct past events on a file system, 2) the accuracy of the reconstruction is comparable to that of human investigators, 3) the accuracy of reconstruction can be increased by using more metadata, and 4) the reconstruction of events is a valuable starting point for further forensic investigations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we automatically reconstruct events that have occurred on the examined device, even if the device was not previously profiled and no log files are available? How can we provide a quick overview of the events to the investigator, without requiring any prior knowledge about the examined system or the applications that were used? And how can we do this without any false positives, so that the investigator can be sure, that the events that are shown are indeed real and relevant for the investigation?
